newsitem.title: USA: Koch Minnesota refinery says operating on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Koch Minnesota refinery says operating on stocks.

text.p: Koch Oil's large refinery in Minnesota is running off stocks after the virtual closure of Canada's Interprovincial Pipeline due to severe weather, a spokesman said Monday.
"We're running the refinery off of inventories but we don't anticipate any short-term impact on our ability to supply fuel to the market place," said Riff Yeager, a spokesman for the plant.
"The variable is how long the line remains down," Yeager added.

The Interprovincial, which with the Lakehead portion on the U.S. side of the border is the world's longest crude oil pipeline system, lost a million barrels per day (bpd) of its 1.4 million bpd on Saturday evening when three pumping stations in Minnesota were hit by a power outage caused by severe snowstorms.
IPL said Monday it expected the pipeline to remain down until at least Wednesday.
The Koch plant at Rosemount, Minn. is one of two in the state and, with crude distillation capacity of about 286,000 barrels a day, accounts for the bulk of the state's 355,000 bpd capacity.
